architecture: v2 (re-root after the heart BLOCK against task242: a pilot county's municipalities qualifying for a 2027 vacant-dwelling activation grant, each dwelling's occupancy in a November fortnight read from its own hourly electricity load beside the population register)
slot_note: re-root of task470 in the same objective (Data Extraction & Conformation), batch 1
niche: register-based dwelling occupancy certified for a grant from the electricity hub's hourly meter loads beside the population register, in a heated Norwegian November
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the registers and the meter reads correctly and reads the scheme's definition takes each dwelling's average daily consumption over the reference fortnight and counts as vacant the dwellings under a consumption floor (the utility-data vacancy rule official statisticians use), or checks only the population register's empty dwellings against their meters, and designates the wrong municipalities, because an empty Norwegian dwelling is heated through November and draws more than many lived-in ones, and dwellings whose registered residents have left still sit on the register.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each municipality's share of dwellings nobody lived in, the register-based dwelling statistic official statistics builds from administrative sources, read here as the presence of a household's daily routine in each dwelling's own hourly load against the heating that runs in an empty home in a Norwegian November; with another field's nouns there is no heated empty dwelling, no population register and no household rhythm inside a meter load, and the task stops reading the same.
layer1: hourly reads in UTC against a local-time household day
meter replacements splitting a dwelling's fortnight across two meter point IDs
estimated hours replaced by measured ones in a later delivery
meter points keyed to addresses with unit numbers written differently from the cadastre's
a municipality renumbered after a boundary change in one register only
holiday homes and dwellings under construction on the cadastre
communal and non-dwelling meter points in the hub's extract
stakeholder_role: the head of the national statistics office's dwelling statistics section, who certifies the pilot county's municipal vacancy shares to the ministry for the 2027 grant

world.geography: Norway (a fictional county of ten municipalities)

driver: The decisive quantity is whether each unit was in use during a window, seen only through a continuous meter whose level is dominated by a load that runs whether or not anyone uses the unit, so use is the presence of the users' daily rhythm in the unit's own record, not the record's level and not an official roll of users, and checking only the roll's empty units misses the units the roll still lists after their users left.
driver_concrete: A dwelling counts as vacant when nobody lived in it in the reference fortnight, whatever the population register shows; an empty Norwegian dwelling is heated through November, so its hourly load runs with the outdoor temperature at levels many lived-in flats never reach, and only a household's daily cycle (the morning and evening rise over the night's level) in its own hourly reads shows that someone lived there; the field's consumption floor finds almost none of the heated empties, and the register's empty dwellings checked against their meters miss the dwellings whose registered residents have moved to care or left.
stump: A competent solver conforms the cadastre, the population register and the hub's hourly reads, takes each dwelling's average daily consumption over the fortnight and counts as vacant the dwellings under a consumption floor, which finds only the unheated empties and designates one municipality; an empty dwelling in a Norwegian November is heated, so its load runs with the outdoor temperature at levels many lived-in flats never reach, and only a household's morning and evening rise over its own night-time level shows that someone lived there, which designates four.

lineage.driver: Activity at each site is seen through a sensor that records every event of some units and none of others, and the units it never records are spread unevenly across sites, so the missing activity is not a fixed share of what the sensor saw: it is rebuilt as the never-recorded units based at each site times the activity per such unit that the fully counted sites show, while one seen-to-counted ratio moves the missing activity from the sites holding those units to the sites whose units are all recorded.

differentiation.task477: task477 measures growth on work done by estimating each unit's exposure to payment schedules from how its sub-period totals move with the payment dates; here nothing is an exposure or a calendar effect: each dwelling's own hourly load is read for a household's daily cycle against the heating that runs in an empty home, to say whether anyone lived there in the fortnight.
